title: toxicodendron discolor
intro: Toxicodendron discolor, commonly known as the poison sumac plant, is a flowering plant native to the southeastern United States. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including treating fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of the plant are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, alkaloids, and terpenoids, that exhibit antioxidant, analgesic, and antiseptic activities. However, despite its potential benefits, the plant's sap contains urushiol, a potent allergen that can cause severe skin irritation and allergic reactions in some individuals.
